observations: Photo 0 is small and low resolution: a desktop photocopier with a document feeder on top, a control panel with buttons and one paper drawer.
The machine is wrapped in clear plastic film, the way dealers re-wrap used imported copiers.
Photo 0 front lower panel shows the 'SHARP' logo; the model text under it is too small and blurred to read.
The casing is off-white or cream with an older styling; no stains or cracks can be seen through the film at this resolution.
No power-on view, display, sample copy, counter or rating plate is shown.

read_from: photo 0 'SHARP' logo on the front lower panel

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a copier; print and scan functions and the model are not shown.
No dirt shows through the plastic film in photo 0, but the photo is too small and blurred to judge the casing, glass or rollers.
Plastic film alone does not prove new; the older styling fits a used import.
Repair history cannot be seen in a photo.
No power-on view or copy test is shown.
No receipt or warranty is shown.

risks.risk: The copier may not power on, may jam, or may print streaked or faint copies.
risks.proof: A clip of it powering on and copying a printed page, with the copy held up to the camera.

risks.risk: Model unknown; Sharp desktop copiers differ in speed and functions, which moves the price.
risks.proof: A close photo of the model badge on the front and the rating plate on the back.
risks.if_unproven: as the most basic Sharp desktop copier, copy only

risks.risk: High page count and worn drum or developer.
risks.proof: A photo of the counter readout on the display or a printed counter report.
risks.if_unproven: as high count with worn drum

risks.risk: Toner cartridge, drum or power cable may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo with the front cover open showing toner and drum in place, and the power cable beside it.

risks.risk: Receipt and warranty may not exist.
risks.proof: A photo of the receipt and warranty beside the rating plate.
risks.if_unproven: as no receipt and no warranty

proof_requests: A close photo of the model badge and the rating plate.
A clip of the copier powering on and making a copy, with the copy shown.
A photo of the counter readout.
A clear photo out of the plastic film, front cover open, with a handwritten note carrying today's date.
response.reason: The Sharp logo is readable in photo 0 and it is plainly a desktop copier, so it can be priced at its worst case as the most basic Sharp desktop copier, not proven working. The model badge and a working copy clip would raise it.
